clue.text: A new tax meeting relative opposition

parts.note: a tithe was a tenth of produce paid as a church tax
sis, short for sister, is a relative

explanation.surface: A fresh levy runs into resistance from a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: An antithesis is a direct contrast or opposite, so it stands for opposition between two ideas.

clue.text: Help put on ace opera

indicators.note: put on in a down clue places the ace letter after (below) the word for help

parts.note: aid means help
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: Assistance is needed to stage a top opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Aida is Verdi's opera set in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Lowest honour having enough power that can be retained

parts.note: in bridge the honour cards are ace, king, queen, jack and ten, the ten being lowest
able means having the power or capacity to do something

explanation.surface: A minor award with the clout to keep its holder in post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowest honour' looks like a modest award; it is the ten, the lowest of bridge's honour cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenable describes a position or post able to be held, kept or defended.

clue.text: Increasing speed on outskirts of Londonderry so as to gain time

parts.note: tempo is speed and rising is increasing, giving tempo rising

indicators.note: outskirts of means the city name contributes only its outermost letters

explanation.surface: Traffic accelerating on the edge of a Northern Irish city.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to stall or delay to gain time, so the adverb means in a stalling way.

clue.text: Record fibres in letters

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
istle is a plant fibre from agave, used for cord and brushes

explanation.surface: A disc of documented fibres is described in correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistles are letters, especially formal ones like those of the New Testament apostles.

clue.text: United goalkeeper's place in line-up not a soul supports

indicators.note: supports in a down clue puts the word for nobody beneath the numeral

parts.note: a goalkeeper wears number one in a football team list, written as the Roman numeral I
not a soul means none

explanation.surface: A football team's keeper is left unsupported by anyone in the line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club name alongside the goalkeeper, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Things joined in one are combined into a single whole, merged together.

clue.text: Old fogey in the same manner as before

indicators.note: as before tells us to give the same piece again, so the ditto short form appears twice

parts.note: do. is the written short form of ditto, meaning in the same manner

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in the past keeps doing things exactly the way they always have.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is the abbreviation of ditto, used in lists to mean the same again; 'as before' repeats it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodo, from the extinct bird, is informal for a stuffy person hopelessly behind the times.

clue.text: Self-inflicted disadvantage of women in stormy lagoon

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for women inside the rearranged lagoon
stormy says the letters of lagoon are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Women caught in a storm on a lagoon have only themselves to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' turns LAGOON into ONGOAL, with W inserted after the first O.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a goal scored into one's own net, the phrase means an act that harms its doer.

clue.text: Working at church Flora, upset, left finally

indicators.note: finally places the left abbreviation at the very end

parts.note: on means working, operating
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: upset means Flora's letters are knocked into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: At a service, Flora is distressed and walks out at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' does double duty: it places L last and is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Once and for all means conclusively, settling a matter finally and permanently.

clue.text: Material study I'm following

indicators.note: following places the words I'm after the room for working

parts.note: a den is a private room for working, a study

explanation.surface: Someone says they are coming after a piece of study material.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton twill fabric, the cloth of jeans.

clue.text: Having nothing of animal or vegetable origin in newspaper I see

definitions.text: Having nothing of animal or vegetable origin

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or periodical speaking for a group
the letter C is pronounced like the word see

explanation.surface: Something with no plant or animal source, as spotted in the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Inorganic matter is mineral, not derived from living things, plant or animal.

clue.text: Fetching a son's grand, being sold for a trifle

parts.note: going for means fetching, going to get
son gives the abbreviation-free word, with 's as 'has'
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A son's piano goes cheaply at the sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetching' suggests attractive, but here it is going to collect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going for a song is being sold very cheaply, for a trifling sum.

clue.text: Expose bold thief falsely entrapping depressed female

indicators.note: entrapping says the scrambled thief encloses the word for depressed, with the female letter tacked on
falsely says the letters of bold thief are put together wrongly, in a new order

parts.note: low means depressed, down in spirits

explanation.surface: A brazen crook caught holding a miserable woman is to be exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falsely' turns BOLD THIEF into BTHELIDOF, which takes LOW after its B; F for female ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow the lid off a scandal is an idiom for revealing it, exposing it publicly.

clue.text: Dance that's hot — fine if daughter's shown the door by clubs

indicators.note: shown the door by means the daughter letter is thrown out and the clubs letter takes its place

parts.note: okey-dokey is jokey slang for fine, OK
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A sizzling dance that's all right if the girl is ejected by the clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The hokey-cokey is the British name for the circle dance Americans call the hokey-pokey.
explanation.definitionFit: The hokey-cokey is a party dance done in a circle with put your left leg in moves.

clue.text: Individual's large vessel is a joke

parts.note: one means a single individual; the 's is just 'has' joining the pieces
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Someone's big ship is a laughing matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-liner is a short quip delivered in a single sentence, a kind of joke.

clue.text: Nimbler and more delicate but not French

indicators.note: but not means the abbreviation for French is taken away from the comparative

parts.note: fragiler is the comparative of fragile, more delicate

explanation.surface: A dancer who is quicker on their feet and more refined, though not from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means nimble, so the comparative of one matches the comparative of the other.

clue.text: This cult society could turn to masochism

indicators.note: could turn to says the answer's letters plus the society letter can be rearranged into masochism

explanation.surface: A cult of tough-guy posturing might slide into self-inflicted pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus S, rearranged, gives MASOCHISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Machismo is an exaggerated cult of masculine toughness, a set of attitudes worshipped like a creed.

clue.text: Master of lengths and angles put cue back with cover on

indicators.note: put back here means set the word cue in reverse order

parts.note: a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A snooker expert replaces his cue and caps it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master of lengths and angles' suggests a snooker player handling a cue, but it is the Greek geometer.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid, the ancient Greek mathematician, set out the classical geometry of lines, lengths and angles.

clue.text: Endless gossip — smile shows embarrassment

indicators.note: Endless means the word for gossip loses its final letter

parts.note: chat is gossip, idle talk
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: Non-stop gossip and a smirk reveal someone's awkwardness.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation from humiliation or disappointment, close kin to mortification.

clue.text: Ride around with learner needing to keep awake

indicators.note: needing to keep says the abbreviations for around and learner hold the word for waking inside them

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means around a date
L is the learner driver's plate letter
rouse means wake up, used as awake (a verb)

explanation.surface: A learner driver on a ride round the block has to stay alert.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousel is a merry-go-round, a fairground ride.

clue.text: Widow dined to gratify fully

parts.note: sati was the old Hindu custom, and the widow who performed it, of self-immolation on a husband's pyre
ate means dined

explanation.surface: A widow eats her fill to be completely satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: To satiate is to satisfy an appetite completely, even to excess.

clue.text: Transplant earth?

parts.note: the letters of heart, once changed around, give the clue word earth

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether to move soil to a new place.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: a change of 'heart' turns it into 'earth'. A heart transplant literally changes a heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart transplant gives a patient a new heart, a literal reading of a phrase meaning changed mind.

clue.text: Some progress for cannibals

indicators.note: some means only part of the word progress is used

explanation.surface: A little advancement for man-eaters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres in folklore are giants who eat people, so they are man-eaters of storybooks.

clue.text: Admit to a band across the middle

definitions.meaning: to own up, confess, as in the informal phrase with up
in heraldry, a broad horizontal band across the centre of a shield

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to a belt around their waist.
explanation.definitionFit: Fess, short for confess, means admit; in heraldry it is the shield's central horizontal stripe.

clue.text: Burial places in Glasgow that could be dark and risky

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the two words may form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Scottish graveyards are gloomy and dangerous places.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirkyard is Scots for a churchyard, a graveyard by the kirk, Scotland's word for church.

clue.text: Talk while stationary

definitions.meaning: to talk formally, deliver a speech
zero rate, no speed at all, so not moving

explanation.surface: Someone speaks while standing still.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer as O (zero) and RATE: a speed of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak at length in public; zero rate of travel means motionless.

clue.text: In Perth not one Chinese male

definitions.text: In Perth not one Chinese male

parts.words: In Perth not one Chinese male
parts.note: in Scots speech, as in Perth, one is yin; the Chinese male principle is the opposite of yin, so it is not that one

explanation.surface: No Chinese man is to be found in the Scottish town of Perth.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth here is the Scottish city, not the Australian one. Scots say yin for one, and in Chinese thought yin pairs with its male opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chinese philosophy the masculine, active, bright principle is the partner of the feminine yin.

clue.text: Guns score disastrously with Southern legislature

indicators.note: disastrously says the letters of the two words end up wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Firearms do terrible damage, with lawmakers from the South involved.
explanation.definitionFit: The US Congress, Senate and House of Representatives together, is the American national law-making body.
